newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols bid as choppy spot pokes at highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols bid as choppy spot pokes at highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were firmer as the spot greenback touched new highs in choppy U.S. trading, dealers said.

Even though the dollar pulled back against the yen, briefly dipping below 118 yen from overnight highs above 119 after a selloff in U.S. asset markets, it quickly bounced off the lows again and discouraged option selling, they added.
"It's been so choppy that you wouldn't want to sell volatilities, even when the dollar is a little lower," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank.

Earlier, as the dollar climbed above 119 yen, the highest level since the May/June slide, trigger prices for some sizeable exotic options were taken out and short-covering linked to hedge positions against those exotics pushed up the three-month area of the volatility curve, he added.
He also noted that the back end, which had led the steady surge in volatilities this week, was fairly stable today, flattening the three-month to one-year part of the curve.
Three-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 11.6/11.8 percent, up from 11.2/11.5 late on Thursday. One-year was up 0.1 point or so at 12.0/12.1 percent.
The front end was bolstered by the choppy spot movement but capped by the weekend time decay pressure. One-month dollar/yen edged up 0.3 point at 11.3/11.6 percent.

Okada said huge mark selling in spot mark/yen was behind the divergence between dollar/yen and dollar/mark in early U.S. business, when the dollar dipped against the yen but pressed higher against the German unit to above 1.86 marks.
Spot mark/yen had been gradually creeping up in the past week, but corporate hedgers still seemed to have plenty of appetite to sell mark/yen on counter-trend bounces, he noted.
Dollar/mark volatilities were generally firmer, with the curve flattening slightly, on the dollar's continued advance.
A hedge fund trader in New York said low delta mark puts in the back end were actively sought.

Some trades were done as far as two-years out, theta-hedged with six-month or one-year, he noted. With delta in some cases below 10, strike prices discussed were now as high as 2.10, or even 2.30, marks.
"It's unbelievable," the hedge fund trader said. "People are buying a lot in the back, and that's eventually going to be pushing up the front end."

Still, the spot dollar's relatively one-way advance with little corrective pullbacks had held actual volatility from surging so far, traders said. They added that was limiting gains in front end implied volatilities and prevented the curve from inverting despite the dollar's 10-pfennig rise in the month of July.
One-month dollar/mark rose more than half a point to 10.4/10.7 percent, while one-year was up 0.3 at 10.6/10.8.
Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, for dollar/mark stood at around 0.6/0.9 point in favor of mark puts in most maturities along the curve.
